evidence.finding: Voice-platform monitoring reported intermittent call-processing delays across all queues at 09:15, exactly matching incident onset.
Service level dropped to 34.78% at 09:15 and remained below the 80% target through 11:45; the post-incident mean was 29.16% versus 88.87% before.
Answered calls fell 30.47%, from 67.6 to 47.0 per interval, while abandonment increased from 2.4 to 30.82 and ASA rose 333.47%.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained at 49, while productive staffing increased slightly after incident onset.
All four queues degraded with unchanged queue staffing, supporting a shared all-queue disruption rather than an isolated queue issue.
Offered volume increased 11.17% after incident onset, amplifying pressure but not explaining the disproportionate throughput collapse.

primary_root_cause_detail: An all-queue voice-platform degradation caused intermittent call-processing delays beginning at 09:15, reducing answered throughput and producing sustained queueing, abandonment, ASA, and service-level deterioration.
recommended_actions: Escalate the 09:15 voice-platform degradation to the telephony provider and preserve platform logs for root-cause analysis.
Implement monitoring for call-processing latency, answered-throughput drops, and simultaneous cross-queue ASA increases.
Activate incident routing or overflow contingencies when an all-queue platform disruption is detected.
Review capacity buffers for moderate demand increases during platform degradation and validate recovery before closing the incident.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Logged-in and scheduled staffing stayed at 49, productive staffing did not decline, and every queue retained its staffed-agent count.
Center AHT decreased 0.24%; queue-level changes were small and mixed.
Degradation affected every queue, transfer rates were stable or lower, and the only visible event was an all-queue platform degradation.
Volume rose only moderately overall, while low-growth queues also deteriorated severely; demand was a contributor rather than the primary cause.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level failure was most likely caused by an all-queue voice-platform degradation beginning at 09:15. Staffing and AHT remained stable, but answered throughput fell sharply while ASA and abandonment surged. An 11% volume increase amplified the impact but was not the primary cause.
